blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, supply chain models are strategic choices, not operational conveniences. Choosing between make-to-stock and make-to-order is not really about manufacturing — it is about who carries which risks, how much working capital is tied up, how much customer variety you can offer, and how fast you can respond when the market shifts. Get the model right for the business you actually want to be, and every operational decision that follows becomes easier. Get it wrong, and the whole organisation spends years fighting against a design choice nobody remembers making.

The senior leader's test is to ask, for each major product line, three questions. What is the natural demand pattern of this product, and how much uncertainty does it carry? What level of service do customers genuinely expect, and what would they pay for? And how much capital are we willing to tie up in inventory to deliver that service level?

The honest answers to these three questions point clearly to the right model — which, more often than most leaders would like to admit, is not the one they are currently running.

items.q: According to the text, the choice between make-to-stock and make-to-order is fundamentally about…
options: reducing headcount on the factory floor
the preferences of the plant managers
risk, working capital, variety and responsiveness
items.why: "it is about who carries which risks, how much working capital is tied up, how much customer variety… and how fast you can respond".

items.q: What three questions does the senior leader's test involve?
options: Supplier price, delivery speed and warranty
Demand pattern and uncertainty, expected service level, and capital tied up in inventory
items.why: O texto lista exatamente essas três perguntas para cada linha de produto.

items.q: What does the phrase "fighting against a design choice nobody remembers making" most strongly suggest?
options: That employees resist all forms of change
That the wrong model quietly constrains the organisation for years
That design choices are irrelevant to performance
That documentation of past decisions is always lost
items.why: Inferência: um modelo mal escolhido vira uma restrição invisível e duradoura que a empresa combate sem saber a origem.

items.q: The final sentence implies that many leaders…
options: refuse to ask the three questions at all
already run the model best suited to their business
are running a model that is not the right one for their business
items.why: Inferência: "is not the one they are currently running" — a resposta honesta costuma apontar para um modelo diferente do atual.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Service expectations should shape the choice of model.
The supply chain model is essentially a manufacturing detail to be delegated.
The right model makes subsequent operational decisions easier.
Getting the model wrong carries a long-lasting cost.
items.why: Inferência: a tese do texto é o oposto — o modelo é uma escolha estratégica de board, não um detalhe operacional a delegar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando as conclusões da revisão à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making time. I'll be direct, because the review has led somewhere uncomfortable. For our largest product line, the make-to-stock model we've run for a decade is the wrong one — and it has been for at least three years.

The demand pattern shifted long ago. Orders are now lumpier, more customised, and far harder to forecast, yet we keep building to stock against a forecast we no longer believe. The result is warehouses full of the wrong variants, and working capital tied up where it earns us nothing.

Had we caught this earlier, the transition would have been gentler. I won't pretend it will be painless now. Moving to a make-to-order model for this line means longer lead times that sales will have to defend, and a period where service dips before it recovers.

But the honest answer to the three questions we always ask points one way. I'd rather we sign off on the harder decision today than spend another three years fighting a design nobody in this room chose on purpose.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What conclusion has Harry's review reached about the largest product line?
options: The make-to-stock model is the wrong one and has been for years
The line should be discontinued entirely
The model is correct but poorly executed
The forecast simply needs to be updated
items.why: "the make-to-stock model we've run for a decade is the wrong one — and it has been for at least three years."

items.q: Why is the current model failing, according to Harry?
options: Demand became lumpier and more customised, yet they keep building to a forecast they no longer trust
items.why: "Orders are now lumpier, more customised… yet we keep building to stock against a forecast we no longer believe."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "Had we caught this earlier, the transition would have been gentler"?
options: Sales should have raised the alarm first
An earlier decision would have made the change less painful than it is now
The team failed to document the original model
items.why: Inferência: o condicional irreal indica arrependimento — agir antes teria suavizado a mudança que agora será dolorosa.

items.q: What trade-off does moving to make-to-order involve for this line?
options: Longer lead times and a temporary dip in service before it recovers
items.why: "longer lead times that sales will have to defend, and a period where service dips before it recovers."

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's stance in this meeting?
options: Candid about the pain, yet firmly advocating the harder decision
Optimistic that the change will be effortless
items.why: Inferência: ele reconhece que não será indolor, mas defende assinar hoje a decisão difícil — franco e decidido.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board treated the model as a strategic choice, not a detail to delegate." A strategic choice is…
options: a high-level decision that shapes the direction of the business
items.why: Strategic choice = escolha estratégica: uma decisão de alto nível que molda o rumo do negócio.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Building ahead of an unreliable forecast leaves ___ tied up in slow-moving inventory."
items.why: Working capital = capital de giro, o dinheiro que fica imobilizado no estoque.

items.q: "For that line, the demand pattern is lumpy and hard to forecast." A demand pattern is…
options: the design of the product itself
the way demand behaves and varies over time
items.why: Demand pattern = padrão de demanda: como a procura se comporta e varia ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Customers expect next-day delivery, so we must hold enough stock to protect that ___."
items.why: Service level = nível de serviço: o grau de disponibilidade/prontidão que o cliente espera.

items.q: "More leaders should be willing to admit that their current model is the wrong one." To admit here means to…
items.why: To admit = admitir, reconhecer como verdadeiro algo desconfortável.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em revisões estratégicas de supply chain. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the model change." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out make-to-order line by line rather than all at once." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Sales pushed back on the longer lead times." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team endorsed the switch but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Trimming safety stock alone won't move the needle on this line's economics." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
